extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists, mathematicians, and developers) who employ the realclassify, rootisolation, and rstandard libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Using SINGULAR library procedures (realclassify.lib, rootisolation.lib, rstandard.lib): their usage signatures, preconditions/assumptions, return values, and recommended setup (monomial orders, base ring characteristics) to compute invariants, isolate real roots, and compute bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: realmorsesplit preconditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristic of the basering must be zero, the monomial order must be local, f must be contained in maxideal(2) and the Milnor number of f must be finite. The Milnor number can be provided as an optional parameter to avoid recomputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: realmorsesplit(f[, mu]); f poly, mu int. Return: a list consisting of the corank of f, the inertia index, an upper bound for the determinacy, and the residual form of f. Example given in documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: realmorsesplit return structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a list consisting of the corank of f, the inertia index, an upper bound for the determinacy, and the residual form of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example output format shown in documentation (e.g., [1]: 2, [2]: 0, [3]: 3, [4]: <residual form>). See also morsesplit reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: milnornumber precondition
rubrics_metrics.description: The monomial order must be local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: milnornumber(f); f poly. Return: Milnor number of f, or -1 if the Milnor number is not finite. Example: milnornumber(x3+y4) -> 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: milnornumber return semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the Milnor number of a polynomial f, or -1 if the Milnor number is not finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other side-effects; requires local monomial order. Example shown in documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: determinacy preconditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristic of the basering must be zero, the monomial order must be local, f must be contained in maxideal(1) and the Milnor number of f must be finite. The Milnor number can be provided as an optional parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: determinacy(f[, mu]); f poly, mu int. Return: an upper bound for the determinacy of f. Example: determinacy(x3+xy3) -> 5. See references to related procedures (highcorner, milnornumber).

rubrics_metrics.name: determinacy return
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an upper bound for the determinacy of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the Milnor number as optional mu avoids recomputation of the Milnor number.

rubrics_metrics.name: addnondegeneratevariables behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds squares of the non-degenerate variables (i.e. var(cr+1), ..., var(nvars(basering)) for corank cr) to the normalform nf, with signs according to the inertia index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: addnondegeneratevariables(NFR); NFR NormalFormEquation. Example shows that the normal form gains z^2 or similar terms consistent with inertia index. See realmorsesplit for relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: rootisolation library purpose and domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Implements an algorithm for real root isolation using interval arithmetic; interval arithmetic and the procedures are intended for rational or real polynomial rings. New type ivmat (matrix of intervals) is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview explains use of interval arithmetic, interval Newton Step and exclusion methods specialized for zero-dimensional radical ideals. References provided for theoretical background.

rubrics_metrics.name: bounds usage and return
rubrics_metrics.description: bounds(a) or bounds(a,b) returns an interval. If size(#)==0 it returns [a,a], else the interval [a,#[1]] (documentation text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage examples: bounds(1) -> [1,1]; bounds(2/3,3) -> [2/3,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: length semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: length(I) returns the Euclidean length of the interval I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show length([-1,3]) -> 4 and length([1/5,1/3]) -> 2/15.

rubrics_metrics.name: boxSet semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: boxSet(B, i, I) returns a new box C where C[i] == I (modifies a single entry of a box).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage examples show constructing boxes and setting individual intervals: boxSet(B,2,bounds(-1,1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: ivmatInit semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ivmatInit(m, n) returns an m x n matrix of [0,0]-intervals (initialises an interval matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure proper structure of ivmat type. Example shows ivmatInit(4,5) printout of zero intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivmatSet semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ivmatSet(A, i, j, I) returns interval matrix A where A[i][j] == I (modifies a single entry of an ivmat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: set A[1,2] to bounds(1,2) and print matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: unitMatrix semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: unitMatrix(n) returns an n x n unit interval matrix (identity matrix of intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unitMatrix(2) and unitMatrix(3) shown in documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ivmatGaussian behavior and return
rubrics_metrics.description: ivmatGaussian(A) inverts an interval matrix using Gaussian elimination in the setting of interval arithmetic. Pivoting is handled as a special case because intervals do not behave like scalars (I/I != [1,1] and I-I != [0,0]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: 0 if A not invertible, (1, Ainv) if A invertible where Ainv is the inverse matrix. Example shows obtaining Jinv and verifying Jinv * J (interval product).

rubrics_metrics.name: evalPolyAtBox semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: evalPolyAtBox(f, B) computes an interval extension of the polynomial f evaluated over box B using interval arithmetic and returns an interval containing all possible values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: evalPolyAtBox(f,B); Example: f = x^2 + y - 1 with B = [-1,1] x [1,3]/2 returns interval [-1/2, 3/2].

rubrics_metrics.name: evalJacobianAtBox semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: evalJacobianAtBox(I, B) evaluates each polynomial of the Jacobian matrix of ideal I at box B using interval arithmetic and returns the interval Jacobian matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage example prints interval entries for Jacobian evaluated at the box.

rubrics_metrics.name: rootIsolationNoPreprocessing assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume I is a zero-dimensional radical ideal. Inputs: I ideal, B list of boxes, eps number. Note: rootIsolationNoPreprocessing does not check input ideal for necessary conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: rootIsolationNoPreprocessing(I, B, eps). Return: (L1, L2) where L1 contains boxes smaller than eps which may contain a root, and L2 contains boxes which contain exactly one element of V(I). Theory: checks boxes for no-root, then applies interval Newton step; if Newton step result is in interior of starting box, box contains unique root.

rubrics_metrics.name: rootIsolation usage and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: rootIsolation(I, [start, eps]) returns (L1, L2) like rootIsolationNoPreprocessing but speeds up computation by preprocessing the starting box through univariate reductions via Groebner elimination (FGLM) to compute smaller starting boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume I is zero-dimensional radical ideal. The algorithm performs Groebner basis computations in basering; it is advised to define I with respect to a fast monomial ordering. The algorithm checks I for suitable number of generators and may attempt to find a suitable Groebner basis or apply triangular decomposition if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: rootIsolationPrimdec behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: rootIsolationPrimdec(I) returns boxes which contain exactly one element of V(I) and speeds up computation/improves output by performing a primary decomposition before root isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume I is a zero-dimensional radical ideal. Primary decomposition uses Gianni-Traeger-Zacharias algorithm. As with rootIsolation, Groebner basis computations are performed and a fast monomial ordering is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: rstandard.borderBasis purpose and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: borderBasis(I) computes and returns a border basis for the ideal I given by its generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: Computes a border basis for the ideal given by the generators in I. Usage example in documentation prints many generators of the resulting border basis. The rstandard library implements Janet and border bases for any ordering using the idea of r-standard bases.
